A patient came in with drooling and refusal to eat after swallowing an object.

Then the X-ray loaded 😭

And a round metal disc appeared at the base of the neck.

Quick diagnosis challenge 🔍

What's the most likely diagnosis?

Wild guesses are welcome 👀

Educational illustration.

Answer: Coin in the oesophagus

👀 What you see:
A face-on metal disc projects at the thoracic inlet. A lateral view helps confirm its location.

🦴 Why it matters:
A coin is likely but a button battery must be excluded.

💊 Treatment:
Drooling with an oesophageal object needs urgent endoscopic assessment. A suspected button battery is an emergency.

A patient came in with painless jaw swelling.

Then the X-ray loaded 😭

And a large dark cavity occupied the back of the lower jaw.

What's the most likely diagnosis? 🩻

Wild guesses are welcome

Follow for a new case every night 🔔

Answer: Odontogenic keratocyst

👀 What you see:
A multilocular lucent lesion occupies the posterior mandible with an associated impacted tooth.

🦴 Why it matters:
This can resemble ameloblastoma. Imaging alone cannot establish the tissue diagnosis.

💊 Treatment:
Specialist assessment and histology guide treatment. Long-term follow-up checks for recurrence.

A patient came in with severe shoulder pain and an arm stuck overhead after a fall.

Then the X-ray loaded 😭

The ball of the shoulder was sitting below its socket.

What's the most likely diagnosis? 🩻

Wild guesses are welcome

Follow for a new case every night 🔔

Answer: Luxatio erecta

👀 What you see:
The ball of the shoulder sits underneath its socket instead of inside it and the arm bone points up past the head.

🦴 Why it matters:
This injury can damage nearby nerves and blood vessels.

💊 Treatment:
Prompt reduction by a trained clinician follows neurovascular assessment. Pulses and nerve function are checked again afterwards.

A patient came in with drooling and refusal to feed after a suspected ingestion.

Then the X-ray loaded 😭

And an open V-shaped metal object with a small coil appeared at the base of the neck.

Quick diagnosis challenge 🔍

What's the most likely diagnosis?

Wild guesses are welcome 👀

Answer: Swallowed safety pin

👀 What you see:
An open pin with a spring coil projects over the upper oesophageal region.

🦴 Why it matters:
A sharp oesophageal object can perforate the wall.

💊 Treatment:
Urgent specialist removal is required. Further imaging may help establish its position.

A patient came in with an arm that still moved at the break a year after the fracture was supposed to heal.

Then the X-ray loaded 😭

The bone had piled up huge lumps of callus around a break that never actually joined.

Quick diagnosis challenge 🔍

What's the most likely diagnosis?

Wild guesses are welcome 👀

Answer: Hypertrophic nonunion

👀 What you see:
Huge lumps of new bone flare out on both sides of the old break but the crack itself still runs straight through and never closes.

🦴 Why it matters:
Persistent fracture movement can prevent union despite abundant callus. Mechanical and biological factors both need assessment.

💊 Treatment:
Improved stability and compression are often central. Grafting and other treatment depend on the individual fracture.

A patient came in with a firm lump in the calf after a remote stay in an endemic area.

Then the X-ray loaded 😭

A long curling calcification ran through the soft tissues beside the bones.

What's the most likely diagnosis? 🩻

Wild guesses are welcome

Follow for a new case every night 🔔

Answer: Dracunculiasis

A long serpentine soft-tissue calcification suggests a calcified Guinea worm remnant.

This is a likely explanation in the exposure context rather than proof of active infection.

An incidental calcified remnant often needs no removal. Symptoms or uncertainty warrant specialist assessment.

A patient came in with a chest injury after a fall at a construction site.

Then the X-ray loaded 😭

And then the chest film answered every question at once.

What's the most likely diagnosis? 🩻

Wild guesses are welcome

Follow for a new case every night 🔔

Answer: Impalement by a metal rod

👀 What you see:
A metal rod projects across the chest. This AP view alone cannot establish its depth or trajectory.

🦴 Why it matters:
In a true impalement uncontrolled removal can trigger major bleeding.

💊 Treatment:
Trauma specialists plan removal under controlled surgical conditions with bleeding control available.

A patient came in with bilious vomiting soon after the first feed.

Then the X-ray loaded 😭

And the very first feed set everything in motion.

Quick diagnosis challenge 🔍

What's the most likely diagnosis?

Wild guesses are welcome 👀

Answer: Duodenal atresia

👀 What you see:
Two upper abdominal gas bubbles suggest a dilated stomach and proximal duodenum.

🦴 Why it matters:
This suggests proximal obstruction. The cropped view cannot establish that the entire distal bowel is gasless.

💊 Treatment:
The newborn needs urgent assessment and stabilisation. Confirmed atresia is repaired surgically.

An older patient came in with a hot swollen knee.

Then the X-ray loaded 😭

And the knee had more going on than just the swelling.

Quick diagnosis challenge 🔍

What's the most likely diagnosis?

Wild guesses are welcome 👀

Answer: Chondrocalcinosis

👀 What you see:
Thin bright calcified lines lie in the knee cartilage and menisci.

🦴 Why it matters:
Cartilage calcification can accompany CPPD. It may be asymptomatic or occur with acute inflammatory arthritis.

💊 Treatment:
Acute attacks may need anti-inflammatory treatment. A hot swollen joint also needs assessment to exclude infection.

A patient came in with upper abdominal discomfort.

Then the X-ray loaded 😭

And then the reason for that discomfort became very clear.

What's the most likely diagnosis? 🩻

Wild guesses are welcome

Follow for a new case every night 🔔

Answer: Swallowed spoon

👀 What you see:
A complete spoon-shaped metal object projects over the expected stomach region.

🦴 Why it matters:
Long rigid objects can fail to pass the duodenum and can injure the gut wall.

💊 Treatment:
Endoscopic retrieval is often needed. Failed retrieval or complications may require surgery.

A patient came in with decades of worsening breathlessness.

Then the X-ray loaded 😭

And then the chest film stopped the room.

What's the most likely diagnosis? 🩻

Wild guesses are welcome

Follow for a new case every night 🔔

Answer: Progressive massive fibrosis

👀 What you see:
Large upper-lung masses sit among small nodules, with rim-calcified hilar nodes and upward hilar retraction.

🦴 Why it matters:
Severe dust-related lung scarring can merge into large masses. Silica exposure also increases tuberculosis risk.

💊 Treatment:
Care focuses on stopping exposure, respiratory support and assessment for complications, including tuberculosis.

A patient came in with a hugely swollen foot.

Then the X-ray loaded 😭

And the foot had a lot more going on than the outside suggested.

Quick diagnosis challenge 🔍

What's the most likely diagnosis?

Wild guesses are welcome 👀

Answer: Mycetoma

👀 What you see:
Marked foot swelling accompanies rounded bone cavities and periosteal new bone.

🦴 Why it matters:
Chronic fungal or bacterial infection can invade bone and cause major disability. Tissue studies identify the organism.

💊 Treatment:
Therapy depends on the organism. Prolonged medication and selected surgery may be needed; advanced disease can require amputation.
